heading: Z-001 — SUPPORT — TTC zone definition
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.02, para. 01; PDF p. 132; printed p. 1222\.
text: A TTC zone is an area of a highway where road user conditions are changed because of a work zone, an incident zone, or a planned special event through the use of TTC devices, uniformed law enforcement officers, or other authorized personnel.
limitations: Interpretive/definitional source material; this clause does not independently establish a plan violation.

heading: Z-002 — SUPPORT — Work zone boundaries
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.02, para. 02; PDF p. 132; printed p. 1222\.
text: A work zone is a highway area with construction, maintenance, or utility work. It extends from the first warning sign or high-intensity rotating, flashing, oscillating, or strobe lights on a vehicle to the END ROAD WORK sign or last TTC device.
limitations: Interpretive/definitional source material; this clause does not independently establish a plan violation.

heading: Z-003 — SUPPORT — Incident zone boundaries
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.02, para. 03; PDF p. 132; printed p. 1222\.
text: An incident zone is an area of a highway where temporary traffic controls are imposed by authorized officials in response to a traffic incident (see Section 6O.01). It extends from the first warning device (such as a sign, light, or cone) to the last TTC device or to a point where road users return to the original lane alignment and are clear of the incident.
limitations: Interpretive/definitional source material; this clause does not independently establish a plan violation.

heading: Z-005 — SUPPORT — Four TTC zone components
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.03, para. 01; PDF p. 133; printed p. 1223\.
text: As needed and based on engineering judgment, a TTC zone is often divided into advance warning, transition, activity, and termination areas (Figure 6B-1; §§6B.04–6B.07).
limitations: Interpretive/definitional source material; this clause does not independently establish a plan violation.

heading: Z-006 — SUPPORT — Advance warning area definition
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.04, para. 01; PDF p. 133; printed p. 1223\.
text: The advance warning area is the section of highway where road users are informed about the upcoming transition and activity areas or incident area.
limitations: Interpretive/definitional source material; this clause does not independently establish a plan violation.

heading: Z-007 — OPTION — Advance warning area forms
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.04, para. 02; PDF p. 133; printed p. 1223\.
text: The advance warning area may vary from a single sign or high-intensity rotating, flashing, oscillating, or strobe lights on a vehicle to a series of signs in advance of the TTC zone activity area.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode work/shadow-vehicle equipment, activity, location, and relationship to lanes; roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations required by Z-007 (Advance warning area forms).

heading: Z-008 — SUPPORT — Transition area definition
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.05, para. 01; PDF p. 133; printed p. 1223\.
text: The transition area redirects road users out of their normal path and usually involves tapers.
limitations: Interpretive/definitional source material; this clause does not independently establish a plan violation.

heading: Z-009 — STANDARD — Required redirection through the transition
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.05, para. 02; PDF p. 133, 134; printed p. 1223, 1224\.
text: Except for mobile operations, when redirection of the road users’ normal path is required, road users shall be directed from the normal path to a new path with appropriate channelizing devices, traffic control devices, and/or TTC methods.
limitations: Stationary/mobile status, required path redirection, and appropriate devices/methods are not encoded in schema 1.0.0.

heading: Z-010 — OPTION — Mobile operation transition alternative
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.05, para. 03; PDF p. 134; printed p. 1224\.
text: Because it is impracticable in mobile operations to redirect the road users’ normal path with stationary channelization, more dominant vehicle-mounted traffic control devices, such as arrow boards, portable changeable message signs, and high-intensity rotating, flashing, oscillating, or strobe lights, may be used instead of channelizing devices to establish a transition area.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode operation duration, stationary/mobile status, and illumination conditions; mounting/support geometry and vertical clearances; arrow-board type, closed-lane identity, equipment, and placement association required by Z-010 (Mobile operation transition alternative).

heading: Z-011 — SUPPORT — Activity area components
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.06, para. 01; PDF p. 134; printed p. 1224\.
text: The activity area is the section of the highway where the work activity takes place. It is comprised of the work space, the traffic space, and the buffer space.
limitations: Interpretive/definitional source material; this clause does not independently establish a plan violation.

heading: Z-012 — SUPPORT — Work space definition and delineation
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.06, para. 02; PDF p. 134; printed p. 1224\.
text: The work space is that portion of the highway closed to road users and set aside for workers, equipment, and material, and a shadow vehicle if one is used upstream. Work spaces are usually delineated for road users by channelizing devices or, to exclude vehicles and pedestrians, by temporary barriers.
limitations: Interpretive/definitional source material; this clause does not independently establish a plan violation.

heading: Z-013 — OPTION — Stationary or moving work space
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.06, para. 03; PDF p. 134; printed p. 1224\.
text: The work space may be stationary or may move as work progresses.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode operation duration, stationary/mobile status, and illumination conditions required by Z-013 (Stationary or moving work space).

heading: Z-014 — GUIDANCE — Separate work spaces within a project
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.06, para. 04; PDF p. 134; printed p. 1224\.
text: Since there might be several work spaces (some even separated by several miles) within the project limits, each work space should be adequately signed to inform road users and reduce confusion.
limitations: The schema has no roadway/approach associations for separated work spaces or engineering determination of adequate warning for each work space.

heading: Z-015 — SUPPORT — Traffic space definition
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.06, para. 05; PDF p. 134; printed p. 1224\.
text: The traffic space is the portion of the highway in which road users are routed through the activity area.
limitations: Interpretive/definitional source material; this clause does not independently establish a plan violation.

heading: Z-016 — OPTION — Incident response staging space
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.06, para. 16; PDF p. 134; printed p. 1224\.
text: When work occurs on a high-volume, highly-congested facility, a vehicle storage or staging space may be provided for incident response and emergency vehicles (for example, tow trucks and fire apparatus) so that these vehicles can respond quickly to road user incidents.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode work/shadow-vehicle equipment, activity, location, and relationship to lanes; traffic volume, capacity, vehicle mix, and operational assessment required by Z-016 (Incident response staging space).

heading: Z-017 — SUPPORT — Termination area definition and limits
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.07, para. 01; PDF p. 135; printed p. 1225\.
text: The termination area is the section of the highway where road users are returned to their normal driving path. The termination area extends from the downstream end of the work area to the last TTC device such as END ROAD WORK signs, if posted.
limitations: Interpretive/definitional source material; this clause does not independently establish a plan violation.

heading: Z-018 — OPTION — Signs announcing normal operations
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.07, para. 02; PDF p. 135; printed p. 1225\.
text: An END ROAD WORK sign, a Speed Limit sign, or other signs may be used to inform road users that they can resume normal operations.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations required by Z-018 (Signs announcing normal operations).

heading: Z-019 — GUIDANCE — Freeway and expressway advance warning extent
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.04, para. 03; PDF p. 133; printed p. 1223\.
text: On freeways and expressways, advance warning sign placement should extend as far as ½ mile or more because drivers are conditioned to uninterrupted flow.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode roadway class and State-highway ownership; roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations required by Z-019 (Freeway and expressway advance warning extent).

heading: Z-020 — GUIDANCE — Urban nearest warning sign placement
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.04, para. 04; PDF p. 133; printed p. 1223\.
text: On urban streets, the distance in feet from the TTC zone to the nearest warning sign should be 4 to 8 times the speed limit in mph. The high end should be used when speeds are relatively high.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode roadway class and State-highway ownership; roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations required by Z-020 (Urban nearest warning sign placement).

heading: Z-020-B — GUIDANCE — Higher-speed urban multiple-sign warning area
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.04, para. 04; PDF p. 133; printed p. 1223\.
text: When two or more advance warning signs are used on higher-speed urban streets, such as major arterials, the advance warning area should extend a greater distance (Table 6B-1).
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode roadway class and State-highway ownership; roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations required by Z-020-B (Higher-speed urban multiple-sign warning area).

heading: Z-021 — OPTION — Single-sign short advance warning area
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.04, para. 05; PDF p. 133; printed p. 1223\.
text: When a single advance warning sign is used (in cases such as low-speed residential streets), the advance warning area may be as short as 100 feet.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode roadway class and State-highway ownership; roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations required by Z-021 (Single-sign short advance warning area).

heading: Z-022 — GUIDANCE — Rural first warning sign placement
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.04, para. 06; PDF p. 133; printed p. 1223\.
text: On rural highways, the effective placement of the first warning sign, in feet, should be 8 to 12 times the speed limit in mph. The source wording “first warning sign” is retained; Table 6B-1 separately defines A, B, and C.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode roadway class and State-highway ownership; roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations required by Z-022 (Rural first warning sign placement).

heading: Z-022-B — GUIDANCE — Open-highway advance warning extent
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.04, para. 06; PDF p. 133; printed p. 1223\.
text: For open-highway conditions, where two or more advance warning signs are normally used, the advance warning area should extend 1,500 feet or more (Table 6B-1).
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations required by Z-022-B (Open-highway advance warning extent).

heading: Z-023 — GUIDANCE — Advance warning spacing adjustments
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.04, para. 07; PDF p. 133; printed p. 1223\.
text: The distances contained in Table 6B-1 are approximate, are intended for guidance purposes only, and should be applied with engineering judgment. These distances should be adjusted for field conditions, if necessary, by increasing or decreasing the recommended distances.
limitations: This clause requires a site-specific engineering judgment/study or review; schema 1.0.0 has no record of that determination.
Schema 1.0.0 does not encode responsible-agency approval and documented engineering decisions required by Z-023 (Advance warning spacing adjustments).

heading: Z-025 — OPTION — Federal advance warning omission option
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.04, para. 09; PDF p. 133; printed p. 1223\.
text: Advance warning may be eliminated when the activity area is sufficiently removed from the road users’ path so that it does not interfere with the normal flow.
limitations: Activity-area removal from the road-user path and its effect on normal traffic flow are not input facts; the omission decision needs site review.
Source reviewer note: Federal baseline retained for comparison; California modifies the omission conditions in CA-001.

heading: Z-026 — GUIDANCE — Federal baseline — advance warning sign spacing
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.04 para. 07; Table 6B-1; §6H.02 para. 01; PDF p. 133, 140, 171; printed p. 1223, 1230, 1261\.
text:
The following sign spacings should be used, subject to engineering judgment and field adjustment; they are not universal mandatory minima. The highway agency or site-road owner determines the federal low/high speed category.

| Roadway | A (ft) | B (ft) | C (ft) |
| :---- | :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Urban, low speed | 100 | 100 | 100 |
| Urban, high speed | 350 | 350 | 350 |
| Rural | 500 | 500 | 500 |
| Expressway/freeway | 1,000 | 1,500 | 2,640 |

A is the distance from the transition or point of restriction to the nearest sign; B is from the nearest to the second sign; C is from the second to the third sign. In this table, “first” means closest to the TTC zone and “third” means farthest upstream. California replaces the speed categories and adds rows in CA-005.
limitations: This clause requires a site-specific engineering judgment/study or review; schema 1.0.0 has no record of that determination.

Schema 1.0.0 does not encode roadway class and State-highway ownership; responsible-agency approval and documented engineering decisions; roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations required by Z-026 (Federal baseline — advance warning sign spacing).

heading: Z-027 — SUPPORT — Component geometry in Figure 6B-1
citation: Federal MUTCD §6B.03 para. 01; Figure 6B-1; PDF p. 133, 137; printed p. 1223, 1227\.
text:
The figure places advance warning upstream of transition, then activity, then termination. The work space and adjacent traffic space are within the activity area. An upstream longitudinal buffer lies between transition and work space; a lateral buffer separates work and traffic spaces. A downstream longitudinal buffer is shown between work space and downstream taper in termination. A shoulder taper is shown upstream of the principal transition.

Longitudinal means along road-user flow; lateral means across it. This is a component illustration, not a requirement to provide every optional buffer; apply §§6B.06–6B.08. California adds references to Tables 6B-2(CA) and 6B-3(CA).
limitations: Interpretive/definitional source material; this clause does not independently establish a plan violation.

heading: Z-028 — GUIDANCE — Position of advance warning signs
citation: Federal MUTCD §6H.02, para. 01; PDF p. 171; printed p. 1261\.
text: Where highway conditions permit, warning signs should be placed in advance of the transition and activity areas at varying distances depending on roadway type, condition, and posted speed. Table 6B-1 contains information regarding the spacing of advance warning signs. Where a series of two or more advance warning signs is used, the closest sign to the transition and activity areas should be placed approximately 100 feet for low-speed urban streets to 1,000 feet or more for freeways and expressways.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode roadway class and State-highway ownership; roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations; taper/device-to-lane associations and intended traffic-path geometry required by Z-028 (Position of advance warning signs).

heading: Z-029 — GUIDANCE — Crossroad and driveway warning
citation: Federal MUTCD §6H.03, para. 02; PDF p. 172; printed p. 1262\.
text: Where traffic can enter a TTC zone from a crossroad or a major (high-volume) driveway, an advance warning sign should be used on the crossroad or major driveway.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode intersection/crossroad/driveway geometry and turning movements; traffic volume, capacity, vehicle mix, and operational assessment; roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations required by Z-029 (Crossroad and driveway warning).

heading: Z-030 — GUIDANCE — Termination sign location
citation: Federal MUTCD §6H.36, para. 01; PDF p. 180; printed p. 1270\.
text: When used, the END ROAD WORK (G20-2) sign (see Figure 6H-1) should be placed near the downstream end of the termination area, as determined by engineering judgment.
limitations: This clause requires a site-specific engineering judgment/study or review; schema 1.0.0 has no record of that determination.
The agency decision to use the termination sign and the accepted near-end placement depend on engineering judgment.

heading: Z-031 — SUPPORT — Warning area movement in mobile operations
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.01, para. 15; PDF p. 237; printed p. 1327\.
text: Mobile operations also include work activities where workers and equipment move along the road without stopping, usually at slow speeds. The advance warning area moves with the work area.
limitations: Interpretive/definitional source material; this clause does not independently establish a plan violation.

heading: Z-032 — SUPPORT — Work beyond the shoulder and warning threshold
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.05, para. 01; PDF p. 240; printed p. 1330\.
text: When work is being performed beyond the shoulders, but within the right-of-way, little or no TTC might be needed. TTC generally is not needed where work is confined to an area 15 feet or more from the edge of the traveled way. However, TTC is appropriate where distracting situations exist, such as vehicles parked on the shoulder, vehicles accessing the worksite via the highway, and equipment traveling on or crossing the roadway to perform the work operations (for example, mowing). A typical application for work beyond the shoulder is shown in Figure 6P-1.
limitations: Interpretive/definitional source material; this clause does not independently establish a plan violation.

heading: Z-033 — STANDARD — Wide paved shoulder — advance warning
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.06, para. 02; PDF p. 240; printed p. 1330\.
text: For short-term through long-term stationary operations, when a paved shoulder 8 feet or more wide is closed, at least one advance warning sign shall be used.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode paved-shoulder width, roadway-edge position, and shoulder occupation; operation duration, stationary/mobile status, and illumination conditions; roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations required by Z-033 (Wide paved shoulder — advance warning).

heading: Z-033-B — STANDARD — Wide paved shoulder — advance channelization
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.06, para. 02; PDF p. 240; printed p. 1330\.
text: For short-term through long-term stationary operations, when a paved shoulder 8 feet or more wide is closed, channelizing devices shall close the shoulder in advance, delineate the beginning of the work space, and direct traffic to remain within the traveled way.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode paved-shoulder width, roadway-edge position, and shoulder occupation; operation duration, stationary/mobile status, and illumination conditions; taper/device-to-lane associations and intended traffic-path geometry required by Z-033-B (Wide paved shoulder — advance channelization).

heading: Z-034 — GUIDANCE — Analyze partial-lane occupation
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.07, para. 02; PDF p. 241; printed p. 1331\.
text: When work occupies part of a lane, traffic volume, vehicle mix (buses, trucks, cars, and bicycles), speed, and capacity should be analyzed to determine whether to close the affected lane.
limitations: This clause requires a site-specific engineering judgment/study or review; schema 1.0.0 has no record of that determination.

Schema 1.0.0 does not encode bicycle-route geometry and bicycle/vehicle operating conditions; work/shadow-vehicle equipment, activity, location, and relationship to lanes; traffic volume, capacity, vehicle mix, and operational assessment required by Z-034 (Analyze partial-lane occupation).

heading: Z-034-B — GUIDANCE — Remaining lane width with encroachment
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.07, para. 02; PDF p. 241; printed p. 1331\.
text: When work occupies part of a lane, the lane should be closed unless the encroachment permits a remaining lane width of 10 feet. See the conditional 9-foot option Z-036 and California restriction CA-009.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode remaining lane width, vehicle mix, and encroachment geometry required by Z-034-B (Remaining lane width with encroachment).

heading: Z-035 — GUIDANCE — Truck off-tracking and minimum lane width
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.07, para. 03; PDF p. 241; printed p. 1331 / Federal MUTCD §6P.01; notes to Figure 6P-43, TA-43, note 1; PDF p. 348; printed p. 1438\.
text: Truck off-tracking should be considered when determining whether the minimum lane width of 10 feet is adequate.
limitations: This clause requires a site-specific engineering judgment/study or review; schema 1.0.0 has no record of that determination.
Schema 1.0.0 does not encode remaining lane width, vehicle mix, and encroachment geometry required by Z-035 (Truck off-tracking and minimum lane width).

heading: Z-036 — OPTION — Federal reduced lane width option
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.07, para. 04; PDF p. 241; printed p. 1331\.
text: A lane width of 9 feet may be used for short-term stationary work on low-volume, low-speed roadways when vehicular traffic does not include longer and wider heavy commercial vehicles.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode roadway class and State-highway ownership; operation duration, stationary/mobile status, and illumination conditions; remaining lane width, vehicle mix, and encroachment geometry required by Z-036 (Federal reduced lane width option).
Source reviewer note: Federal baseline retained for comparison; California narrows the option in CA-009.

heading: Z-037 — GUIDANCE — Median work proximity threshold
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.08, para. 02; PDF p. 241; printed p. 1331\.
text: If work in the median of a divided highway is within 15 feet from the edge of the traveled way for either direction of travel, TTC should be used through the use of advance warning signs and channelizing devices.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations; taper/device-to-lane associations and intended traffic-path geometry required by Z-037 (Median work proximity threshold).

heading: Z-038 — OPTION — Additional interior-lane closure for lateral clearance
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.11, para. 09; PDF p. 243; printed p. 1333\.
text: For work on a multi-lane, non-access-controlled road, when closing a left-hand lane on a multi-lane undivided road, as vehicular traffic flow permits, the two interior lanes may be closed, as shown in Figure 6P-30, to provide drivers and workers additional lateral clearance and to provide access to the work space.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode mounting/support geometry and vertical clearances; traffic volume, capacity, vehicle mix, and operational assessment required by Z-038 (Additional interior-lane closure for lateral clearance).
Schema 1.0.0 has no numbered typical-application/layout identifier; closure type alone does not establish this source trigger.

heading: Z-039 — STANDARD — Centerline delineation for left-lane closure
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.11, para. 10; PDF p. 243; printed p. 1333\.
text: For work on a multi-lane, non-access-controlled road, when only the left-hand lane is closed on undivided roads, channelizing devices shall be placed along the center line as well as along the adjacent lane.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode taper/device-to-lane associations and intended traffic-path geometry required by Z-039 (Centerline delineation for left-lane closure).

heading: Z-040 — GUIDANCE — Adjacent lane closure consideration
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.11, para. 11; PDF p. 243; printed p. 1333\.
text: For work on a multi-lane, non-access-controlled road, when an interior lane is closed, an adjacent lane should also be considered for closure to provide additional space for vehicles and materials and to facilitate the movement of equipment within the work space.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode work/shadow-vehicle equipment, activity, location, and relationship to lanes required by Z-040 (Adjacent lane closure consideration).

heading: Z-041 — GUIDANCE — Intersection cross-street warning
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.12, para. 06; PDF p. 244; printed p. 1334\.
text: For work at an intersection, advance warning signs, devices, and markings should be used on all cross streets, as appropriate.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode intersection/crossroad/driveway geometry and turning movements; roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations; pavement marking identity, condition, conflicts, and placement required by Z-041 (Intersection cross-street warning).

heading: Z-041-B — GUIDANCE — Intersection warning above 40 mph
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.12, para. 06; PDF p. 244; printed p. 1334\.
text: For intersection work, additional advance warning signs should be used when the posted speed limit, pre-work off-peak 85th-percentile speed, or anticipated speed exceeds 40 mph. The typical applications depict urban arterial intersections.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode roadway class and State-highway ownership; intersection/crossroad/driveway geometry and turning movements; mounting/support geometry and vertical clearances required by Z-041-B (Intersection warning above 40 mph).

heading: Z-042 — OPTION — Restricted near-side advance warning space
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.12, para. 10; PDF p. 244; printed p. 1334\.
text: Where space is restricted in advance of near-side work spaces, as with short block spacings, two warning signs may be used in the advance warning area, and a third action-type warning or a regulatory sign (such as Keep Left) may be placed within the transition area.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations; taper/device-to-lane associations and intended traffic-path geometry required by Z-042 (Restricted near-side advance warning space).

heading: Z-043 — GUIDANCE — Far-side lane closure starts before intersection
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.12, para. 12; PDF p. 244; printed p. 1334\.
text:
When a lane through an intersection must be closed on the far side, it should also be closed on the near-side approach to preclude merging movements within the intersection.

Z-044 (§6N.12 para. 13\) permits a near-side mandatory turn lane where significant turns occur.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode intersection/crossroad/driveway geometry and turning movements required by Z-043 (Far-side lane closure starts before intersection).

heading: Z-044 — OPTION — Near-side mandatory turn lane option
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.12, para. 13; PDF p. 244; printed p. 1334\.
text: If there are a significant number of vehicles turning from a near-side lane that is closed on the far side, the near-side lane may be converted to a mandatory turn lane.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode work/shadow-vehicle equipment, activity, location, and relationship to lanes required by Z-044 (Near-side mandatory turn lane option).

heading: Z-045 — GUIDANCE — Assess freeway and expressway queues
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.13, para. 03; PDF p. 245; printed p. 1335\.
text: For lane closures on freeways or expressways that may create queues, expected queue length should be assessed during TTC plan design.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode roadway class and State-highway ownership required by Z-045 (Assess freeway and expressway queues).

heading: Z-045-B — GUIDANCE — Adjust freeway and expressway warning for queues
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.13, para. 03; PDF p. 245; printed p. 1335\.
text: For lane closures on freeways or expressways that may create queues, adjustments to sign spacing and sign count, and use of more conspicuous devices, should be considered to increase the advance warning area’s distance and conspicuity.
limitations: This clause requires a site-specific engineering judgment/study or review; schema 1.0.0 has no record of that determination.

Schema 1.0.0 does not encode roadway class and State-highway ownership; roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations required by Z-045-B (Adjust freeway and expressway warning for queues).

heading: Z-046 — STANDARD — Separate opposing traffic on a divided-roadway closure
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.14, para. 02; PDF p. 245, 246; printed p. 1335, 1336\.
text: When two-lane, two-way traffic is maintained on one roadway of a normally divided highway, opposing traffic shall be separated throughout the two-way operation by temporary traffic barriers (concrete safety-shape or approved alternate), channelizing devices, Narrow Two-Way Traffic (W6-4) signs on flexible supports (§6H.17), or a temporary raised island.
limitations: The schema cannot identify normally divided roadway status or the opposing-flow separation method.

heading: Z-046-B — STANDARD — Signing and markings alone do not provide separation
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.14, para. 02; PDF p. 245, 246; printed p. 1335, 1336\.
text: When two-lane, two-way traffic is maintained on one roadway of a normally divided highway, markings and complementary signing shall not be used by themselves for opposing-flow separation.
limitations: The schema cannot identify the two-way divided-roadway operation or whether markings/signs are the only separation.

heading: Z-047 — STANDARD — Prevent queues across tracks
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.17, para. 01; PDF p. 246; printed p. 1336 / §8A.13; PDF pp. 377–378; Figure 6P-46; PDF p. 355\.
text: Where a grade crossing is within or near a TTC zone, lane restrictions, flagging, or other operations shall not create conditions that queue vehicles across the tracks.
limitations: Grade-crossing geometry and an actual queue crossing the tracks are not encoded; predictions are not compliance evidence.

heading: Z-047-B — STANDARD — Control unavoidable track-crossing queues
citation: Federal MUTCD §6N.17, para. 01; PDF p. 246; printed p. 1336 / §8A.13; PDF pp. 377–378; Figure 6P-46; PDF p. 355\.
text: If queuing across tracks cannot be avoided at a grade crossing within or near a TTC zone, a uniformed law enforcement officer or flagger shall be provided at the crossing to prevent vehicles from stopping on the tracks, even when automatic warning devices are present.
limitations: Unavoidable crossing queues and crossing-specific officer/flagger control are not encoded.

heading: Z-048 — OPTION — TA-1 warning omission offset
citation: Federal MUTCD §6P.01; notes to Figure 6P-1, TA-1, note 3; PDF p. 260; printed p. 1350\.
text: In TA-1, the ROAD WORK AHEAD sign or Workers (W21-1a) sign may be omitted where the work space is behind a barrier, more than 24 inches behind the curb, or 15 feet or more from the edge of any roadway.
limitations: Schema 1.0.0 does not encode barrier identity, crashworthiness, delineation, and traffic-path relationship; roadway applicability, approach inventory, and warning-sign/closure associations required by Z-048 (TA-1 warning omission offset).
Schema 1.0.0 has no numbered typical-application/layout identifier; closure type alone does not establish this source trigger.
